post.summary: Sign the club in and obtain a club access/refresh token pair
post.description: Club accounts only: a player's email and password are refused with `invalid_credentials`, exactly as a stranger's are.

post.summary: Rotate the club's access and refresh tokens
Sign the club out: revoke its refresh token (idempotent)
Forgot password?: email the club a link and a code
post.description:
Sends an email with a button and an 8-character code, valid for **one hour** and usable once. The button opens the club website's own `/reset/<token>` page; the code does the same from wherever the person asked.

**Nobody can use this to learn who has an account**: the answer is `202` with no body for an address with an account, without one, and for one asked for too often. **Throttled per address** — past three emails in an hour, a request sends nothing and says so to nobody. A newer email replaces the older one's link and code.

202.description: Accepted — **the same answer whether or not the address has an account**, and whether or not an email was sent.

post.summary: Exchange the club's emailed code for a ticket
post.description:
The address and the code from the email, exchanged for a short-lived `ticket` the new password is then set with. A claim is not a use: until a password is set, the same code can be claimed again.

Only a **right** code learns why it cannot be used; a wrong one is `code_incorrect` whatever else is true.

400.description: `code_incorrect` (`details.field`: `code`) — not the code sent to that address, **or nothing was sent to it**: the two are one answer. Five wrong codes lock the credential.

409.description: The code is right, and it can no longer be used: `credential_expired` (ask again), `credential_used` or `credential_locked` (five wrong codes).

post.summary: Set the club's new password, sign out everywhere, and sign in
post.description: Sets the new password with **exactly one** of the email's link `token` or a claimed code's `ticket`, then **signs out everywhere** and signs this session in: every access token issued before this moment is refused (`access_token_revoked`) and every refresh token revoked, so another browser still signed in is signed out on its next request. The answer is this session's new token pair. The link, the code and the ticket are spent.

400.description: `password_too_weak` (`details.field`: `password`) — 8 to 128 characters with a letter and a digit. The link and the code still work.

404.description: `credential_not_found` — a link or a ticket this surface never issued.

409.description: `credential_expired` (ask again), `credential_used`, `credential_locked`, or `ticket_expired` — the code was right and the password came too late; claiming the code again is a fresh ticket.

post.summary: Sign a club up, with the account its desk signs in with
post.description: Creates the club and its account **together, in one transaction**. There is no verification step. The account then signs in at `POST /api/v1/club/auth/login` — this route issues no tokens.

400.description: A field the desk has to correct, named by `details.field` — the five details' codes, and `email_invalid` or `password_too_weak`. Every field is checked before the email is looked up.

409.description: `club_email_already_registered` — another club's account signs in with this email; `details.field` is `email`. A player holding the same address is never a conflict.

put.description: A full replacement of the five details, at any time. Saving them unchanged records nothing. **A sport an official group declares cannot be unticked**, and the refusal names the group. Answers the details as recorded — names trimmed and collapsed, sports in the registry's order.

400.description: A field the desk has to correct, named by `details.field`: `club_name_invalid`, `club_district_invalid`, `club_city_invalid`, `club_sports_required` or `club_point_invalid`. Nothing was recorded. The website writes the sentence under that field.

409.description: `club_sport_declared_by_group` — the save unticks a sport an official group at the club declares; `details.field` is `sports`, `details.sport` the sport and `details.group` the group's name (the first by name, where several play it). Nothing was recorded. The group's administrator changes its sports first, or the sport stays ticked.

get.summary: The club's administrators, and where each one stands

post.summary: Invite an administrator by name and email
post.description: Emails the person through the mail queue, in this request's transaction. **A new person** gets a button to the public site's `/invite/<token>` and an 8-character code, valid 72 hours; **an existing account** gets *"[Club] wants to make you an administrator"* and a button that opens the app, with no code. Inviting somebody this club removed invites them again.

400.description: A field the desk has to correct, named by `details.field`: `administrator_name_invalid` or `email_invalid`. Nothing was recorded and nothing was sent.

409.description: `administrator_already_invited` — that email is invited here, expired included: resend instead — or `administrator_already_active`. `details.field` is `email`.

post.summary: Resend an invitation: a fresh 72 hours
post.description: For somebody `INVITED` or `EXPIRED`. The email is the original's again, with a new link and code where it carries them; the older ones stop working.

404.description: `administrator_not_found` — no administrator of this club has that id: another club's, a removed one, or none.

409.description: `administrator_already_active` — there is nothing left to open.

post.description: **Only for an account that holds nothing but administrator profiles** — `can_reset_password` on the row. Clears the password, signs the account out everywhere, and puts the person back to `INVITED` with a fresh 72-hour email carrying the invitation's own link and code.

404.description: `administrator_not_found` — no administrator of this club has that id: another club's, a removed one, or none.

409.description: `administrator_also_plays` — the account also plays, and only its owner resets it, through *Forgot password?*; or `administrator_has_no_account` — nobody has set a password yet: resend instead. Nothing moved.

delete.description: The administrator profile ends: the person's next administrator request is refused with `not_an_administrator`. Their player profile and their sessions are untouched, and an invitation still in their inbox opens nothing.

404.description: `administrator_not_found` — no administrator of this club has that id: another club's, a removed one, or none.

get.summary: The club's official groups, and how much of each WhatsApp crowd arrived
get.description: *Official groups at [club]*: each one's name and monogram, who runs it — or `null`, *needs an administrator* — its players and how many are waiting, *From WhatsApp* as players of the WhatsApp group's size, and how many games it gave birth to. By name.

put.summary: Hand an official group over to one of the club's administrators
put.description: Any official group of the club, **one that needs an administrator included**, to any **active** Administrator. Only who answers changes: the link, who can join, the WhatsApp size, the players and **the requests waiting** all stay, and the new Administrator finds them. The previous one stops seeing it — and stays in it if they joined it as a player. Handing it to whoever runs it changes nothing. Answers the group's row as the table now reads it.

404.description: `group_not_found` — not an official group of this club: no such group, a player group whose home club this is, or another club's. Nothing was recorded.

409.description: `administrator_not_active` — the one chosen is not an active Administrator of this club: still invited, expired, removed, another club's, or nobody. Nothing was recorded; choose again from the Administrators table as it stands.

name.title: Name
name.description: As the club typed it: trimmed and collapsed.

status.description: `ACTIVE` once the invitation was taken up; `INVITED` until then; `EXPIRED` once its 72 hours have passed unanswered — resendable.

last_used_at.title: Last Used At
last_used_at.description: On an `ACTIVE` row: when the administrator profile was last used, **to the hour** — *today*, *this week*. `null` otherwise.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: On an `INVITED` row, when it expires; on an `EXPIRED` row, when it did. `null` on an `ACTIVE` row.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: The official groups this administrator runs now, by name — the row's dropdown. **Only on an `ACTIVE` row**: empty for somebody invited, expired or put back to invited by *Reset password*, whose groups read *needs an administrator* on the Groups table meanwhile.

can_reset_password.title: Can Reset Password
can_reset_password.description: Whether *Reset password* may be pressed: only for an account that holds nothing but administrator profiles. Pressing it anyway is `409 administrator_also_plays` or `administrator_has_no_account`.

AdministratorSchema.title: AdministratorSchema
AdministratorSchema.description:
One row of the club's Administrators table (``docs/adr/0184`` §1).
**Every status is derived**, and so is whether *Reset password* is drawn.

AdministratorStatus.title: AdministratorStatus
AdministratorStatus.description: What the Administrators table says of somebody, now.

ClaimCodeRequest.title: ClaimCodeRequest
ClaimCodeRequest.description:
The address and the 8-character code from the email. The code is read
forgivingly — case, spaces and dashes are ignored — and its length is not
checked here: a code of the wrong length is simply not the right code, and
is told ``code_incorrect`` as every other one is. The bound is a cap on
what a request may carry, not a rule about codes.

ticket.title: Ticket
ticket.description: Present it as `ticket` when setting the new password. Good for `expires_in` seconds, and never past the code's own hour; claiming the code again replaces it.

ClaimTicketResponse.title: ClaimTicketResponse
ClaimTicketResponse.description: A correct code, exchanged for a ticket the new password is set with.

name.title: Name
name.description: Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 2–80 characters. Never unique. Refused with `club_name_invalid`.

district.title: District
district.description: As the desk writes it, 2–64 characters. `club_district_invalid`.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: The sports the club offers — at least one, `club_sports_required` otherwise. A sport ticked twice is ticked once, and the answer lists them in the registry's order.

point.description: The map pin. Off the globe is `club_point_invalid`.

ClubDetailsRequest.title: ClubDetailsRequest
ClubDetailsRequest.description:
The five details, **all of them on every save** — the club website edits
them on one page, and a save is a full replacement.

ClubDetailsResponse.title: ClubDetailsResponse
ClubDetailsResponse.description: A club as the desk sees it.

id.title: Id
id.description: The administratorship — the `id` of their row on the Administrators table, and what a handover names.

name.title: Name
name.description: **The name the club gave them**, whole — the one its Administrators table prints beside the same person.

ClubGroupAdministratorSchema.title: ClubGroupAdministratorSchema
ClubGroupAdministratorSchema.description: The Administrator running a group, as the club's own tables name them.

administrator.description: Who runs it now. **`null` while it needs an administrator** — the club removed whoever ran it, and nobody has been handed it: players read *[club] approves joins* and its requests wait, until a handover.

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: *Players*: every Group member — an Administrator who joined it as a player included. **The same number the group page shows**, whoever reads it.

waiting_count.title: Waiting Count
waiting_count.description: How many Join requests are waiting — the amber *N waiting*. `0` when nobody is.

whatsapp_size.title: Whatsapp Size
whatsapp_size.description: How many people the WhatsApp group it mirrors has — *of 48*.

whatsapp_percent.title: Whatsapp Percent
whatsapp_percent.description: *From WhatsApp*: `member_count` over `whatsapp_size`, as a whole percent rounded half up — *11 of 48 · 23%*. **Never capped**: more players than the WhatsApp group has is the real figure, *52 of 48 · 108%*, and the bar is drawn full.

games.title: Games
games.description: How many games **the group gave birth to** — never a game two of its members arranged elsewhere. No group picks a game yet, so `0`; the day one can, it counts them and means the same.

ClubGroupSchema.title: ClubGroupSchema
ClubGroupSchema.description: One row of the club's Groups table: an official group at the club.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: **Every official group at the club**, whoever runs it or nobody, by name. A player group whose home club this is is not the club's, and is never here. Empty before an Administrator makes the first.

name.title: Name
name.description: Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 2–80 characters. Never unique. Refused with `club_name_invalid`.

district.title: District
district.description: As the desk writes it, 2–64 characters. `club_district_invalid`.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: The sports the club offers — at least one, `club_sports_required` otherwise. A sport ticked twice is ticked once, and the answer lists them in the registry's order.

point.description: The map pin. Off the globe is `club_point_invalid`.

email.title: Email
email.description: Unique among club accounts, and may also belong to an unrelated player. Malformed is `email_invalid`; another club's is `409 club_email_already_registered`.

password.title: Password
password.description: 8–128 characters with a letter and a digit — the player's rule. `password_too_weak` otherwise.

ClubSignUpRequest.title: ClubSignUpRequest
ClubSignUpRequest.description:
A club signs up: its details, and the email and password its desk signs
in with. **No second password field** — the website asks once.

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every error response, on both API surfaces.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable identifier for this exact failure. The only half of the envelope a client may branch on.
code.title: Code

message.description: Human-readable diagnostic. Never the copy shown to a user — that is the client's, chosen from the code.
message.title: Message

trace_id.description: This request's identifier, also returned on the X-Request-ID header. Ties a client-side failure to a server log without logging a payload.
trace_id.title: Trace Id

details.description: Structured context for this code, when the code defines any.
details.title: Details

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

ForgotPasswordRequest.title: ForgotPasswordRequest
ForgotPasswordRequest.description: *Forgot password?*: the address to send a link and a code to.

administrator_id.title: Administrator Id
administrator_id.description: An **active** Administrator of the club — the `id` of an `ACTIVE` row on the Administrators table. Anybody else is `409 administrator_not_active`.

name.title: Name
name.description: Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 2–64 characters — `administrator_name_invalid` otherwise. It becomes the person's Name if they are new to Raketa.

email.title: Email
email.description: Malformed is `email_invalid`. Already invited here — expired included — is `409 administrator_already_invited`; already active here is `409 administrator_already_active`.

InviteAdministratorRequest.title: InviteAdministratorRequest
InviteAdministratorRequest.description:
*+ Add administrator*: a name and an email, and nothing else — the club
never sets, sees or handles a password or a code.

MapPointSchema.title: MapPointSchema
MapPointSchema.description: Where the club is: the pin as the desk dropped it, never rounded.

letters.title: Letters
letters.description: The first character of each of the first two words, as typed, or the first two characters of a one-word name: *my raketa group* is `mr`, *Ogrody 33 Club* is `O3`. Draw it as it comes — never change its case.

colour.title: Colour
colour.description: A colour **key** from 0 to 7, fixed for the group for ever — derived from its id, so a rename keeps it. Map it to your own palette; the backend never names a colour.

MonogramSchema.title: MonogramSchema
MonogramSchema.description:
The group's tile, **cut by the backend** so every client draws the same
one (``docs/adr/0183`` §5).

NewPasswordRequest.title: NewPasswordRequest
NewPasswordRequest.description:
The new password, and **exactly one** of what opens the way to it: the
`token` from the email's link, or the `ticket` a claimed code returned.

The password carries no bound here, deliberately: the rule every account
shares — 8 to 128 characters with a letter and a digit — is refused as
`password_too_weak` naming the field, not as a validation error naming none.
Sending both or neither of `token` and `ticket` is a malformed request rather
than a person's mistake, and is the one refusal here that is a `422`.

Sport.description: The four sports Raketa rates, as a closed enum.
